rationale: C06 is a compelling drafting template: the child's operative clause closely reproduces its wording and sequence—directing display of the flag on all Government buildings on a dated Flag Day, then calling upon the people to observe the day with special ceremonies expressing reverence for the flag and its ideals. C10 and C21 are also closely related annual Flag Day precedents, but their operative language is less nearly identical to the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings on Flag Day, Thursday, June 14, 1956, and I call upon the people to observe that day with special ceremonies designed to give expression to our love for our country's flag and our reverence for the ideals for which it stands
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings on Flag Day, Thursday, June 14, 1951, and I call upon the people to observe that day with special patriotic ceremonies designed to give expression to our reverence for the flag and the ideals it symbolizes
shared_material.explanation: The operative provision is almost verbatim, with the year and a few descriptive phrases updated.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 3, 1949 (63 Stat. 492), has formally designated June 14 as Flag Day and has requested the President to issue annually a proclamation calling for the observance of that day
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Congress, by a joint resolution approved on August 3, 1949 (63 Stat. 492), has set aside June 14 of each year as Flag Day
shared_material.explanation: Both invoke the same statutory basis as part of the same annual-proclamation structure.
